And pointed out Judas as the author of the crime.  
While praying for all, you gave thanks,  
And immediately went out and entered the garden.

Night had closed out the light; everyone departed,  
And Jesus began, in distress, to be afraid.  
He tells the disciples to sit for a little while,  
So that he may have time to pray.

Behold, Jesus is read to be trembling and sorrowful.  
Therefore let no one presume to be indignant  
If he sees someone troubled by sorrow;  
Rather, let him strive piously to console him.

## The Sweat of Blood

Then, going a little ahead, he prostrated himself upon the ground  
And asked that the cup be taken from him;  
But he entrusted the matter to the Father’s will.  
Behold, immediately a bloody sweat poured forth.

Has any mortal ever been heard  
To shed bloody sweat because of the horror of death?  
By this, perhaps, Scripture instructs the reader  
That he had never endured a sorrow like it.

## The Arrest

**[Col. 0594C]**

At once the betrayer arrives and is surrounded by many,  
So that the innocent man may be handed over to the hands of the impious.  
He deceitfully kisses Jesus in greeting,  
But Jesus addresses him in words of great gentleness.

“What have you come for, friend?” says the Lord.  
“Have you come to betray with a kiss the one whom you have already sold?”

At once the attendants rush forward in violence  
And do not hesitate to become the slayers of Christ.  
Who could sufficiently marvel at the Savior in this event,  
And at the wondrous sweetness of his heart?

Behold, he calls the man a friend who is worse than his enemies,  
Allowing the betrayer to approach the kiss of peace.  
O most wretched Judas, why did you act thus?  
With a kiss you handed the peaceful one over to death.

Why, abusing Christ’s benefits in this way,  
Were you not ashamed to repay good with evil?  
When the attendants, addressed by his gentlest voice,  
Were asked whom they sought, they immediately fell prostrate.

From this let them consider how harsh the voice of the angry one will be,  
When they could not endure his gentle words.

At last, having been seized, he is wickedly mistreated,  
Given over to terrible bonds and dreadful servitude.  
Thus he is truly compared with the gentlest lamb,  
Who neither utters threats nor resists.

Most gentle Savior, how badly you are tormented!  
Now you are abandoned alone and attacked alone.  
The disciples flee; you alone are held back;  
You are defiled by various insults and spitting.

## The Flight of the Disciples

**[Col. 0595A]**

Come now: where are you fleeing, or where are you hiding,  
You who recently boasted that you would die with the Lord?  
But he first undergoes death freely on behalf of all,  
So that afterward you may not fear dying for him.

## Peter’s Denial

Peter, following, entered the courtyard from a distance,  
But at the voice of a woman denied Jesus three times.  
When he looked upon Jesus, he sighed with weeping  
And atoned for his sins with bitter tears.

## Judas’s Despair

Afterward, when the betrayer saw that Jesus was condemned,  
He returned the silver for which he had sold him;  
Then, departing, the wretched man strangled himself with a noose.  
Thus the robber receives a fitting reward for his payment.

## The Injuries Inflicted on Christ

**[Col. 0595B]**

The entire sleepless night was thus spent;  
No rest whatsoever was granted to Jesus.  
The impious crowd of attendants insults him;  
The innocent man is treated with slaps and blows.

## The Unjust Accusation

False witnesses are brought forward against you, Jesus.  
You remain silent and disregard everything they say.  
When morning comes, bonds are tied around your hands;  
You are dragged to Pilate, and your enemies follow.

You are wickedly accused, but nothing is proved;  
Lies are fabricated, while the truth is concealed.  
Nor was it hidden from the judge what fraud was accomplishing.  
Therefore the governor feared destroying you.

Afterward you are brought before Herod’s presence,  
And questioned with many words while remaining silent.  
The king, indignant, despises you with his army;  
You are led back to the governor dressed in a white garment.

Then the Jews press their accusations more fiercely,  
Rejoicing in the alliance of Herod and the governor.  
You patiently endure dogs barking at you  
And tearing you with unjust words.

The judge marvels at you, silent in all things,  
And tries to rescue Jesus from them.  
But a great tumult of the people is stirred up,  
And the voice of the crowd resounds that he should be crucified.

O most wicked people, why did you act thus?  
Denying the Savior, you asked for an impious man;  
Choosing a robber, you destroyed Christ.  
Thus you deserved, rightly, to be despised by him.

## The Impious Sentence

At last, seeing that he could accomplish nothing  
But was instead increasing the tumult among the people,  
The judge decided that what they requested should be done.  
The faithless people exult; his own people grieve.

## The Flagellation

He is handed over to the soldiers and bound with cords;  
He is placed at the column and harshly scourged;  
His body is bloodied on every side by blows.  
Piety is buried; fury rules.

Behold the tender flesh of the gracious Savior,  
Wickedly fastened to the column with straps;  
Thus it is beaten by the whips of the impious torturer  
That traces of blood remain visible even now.

## Various Insults

**[Col. 0596A]**

After the battle of the blows, see what takes place:  
He is clothed in purple and crowned with thorns;  
A reed is placed in his right hand like a scepter;  
And, mocked, he is worshiped with bended knees.

They spit upon him whom they have mockingly worshiped, striking his face.  
They beat his head with a reed, saying:  
“Prophesy, tell us who struck you.”  
With such mockeries they persist in derision.

O how long it would be to recount each detail!  
But how much longer it was to endure so much!  
It is clear that one labors under deadly harshness  
Who neglects to love the one who loves him in such a way.

Behold, after so many afflictions and insults,  
The bitterness of punishments arises again.  
Why is the punishment recognized as so bitter,  
When what has happened afterward is considered too little?

## The Carrying of the Cross

For Jesus proceeded through the middle of the city  
And carried the instrument of death upon his shoulders.  
The people streamed toward the gates and entrances,  
And his humiliation was visible to everyone.

Come now, soul, look upon the one who loves you,  
Hastening to the gallows for your sake with thanksgiving.  
Look upon your Bridegroom carrying the cross,  
Atoning for your crimes by his punishments.

I see three crowds following you:  
The first, namely, the executioners pressing you forward;  
The second, the Jews, utterly mocking you;  
The third, your friends, grieving anxiously.

## The Crucifixion

**[Col. 0596C]**

At last they proceed to the place of Calvary,  
And there Jesus is stripped of his garments,  
So that each of the soldiers may receive a portion by lot.

*[The supplied source ends here.]*
After this, he is constrained upon the gallows of the cross.

To complete the shame, my Jesus, you are stripped naked,  
so that you may be exposed naked to the winds and cold.  
Though innocent, you are condemned on the cross with the impious,  
and placed in the midst as though you were the leader of criminals.

Your kinsmen stand far off; you are consoled by no one.  
Rather, those by whom you are tortured stand all around you.  
You are blasphemed by malicious, treacherous servants,  
and—what is almost worse—you are abandoned by your own.

O heart swelling with pride, learn not to be puffed up,  
[Col. 0596D] nor, I beg you, be reluctant to imitate Jesus,  
whom you see being treated shamefully and vilely,  
though he deserved always to be honored above all.

Learn to despise the false favor of honor  
and to scorn the praises of human approval.  
When people, seeing you outwardly, regard you as vile,  
consider yourself vile in the eyes of the Creator.

Why, then, wretched one, do you murmur and grow indignant  
if you are regarded as vile before human beings,  
and are even more reproved in the eyes of God,  
before whom you are proved vile according to your merits?

With his arms stretched out far, his hands are nailed through;  
his skin and flesh are pierced by three nails.  
His nerves and veins are torn in the same manner,  
yet the treacherous are not satisfied even with such punishments.

[Col. 0597A] But, so that nothing might be lacking to the horror of death,  
iron penetrating his feet increases the pain.  
Thus the impious sharpen their fury,  
wickedly setting aside fear of the Lord.

They strike terror with the sounding hammers,  
piercing all the skin together with the flesh,  
lacerating the nerves and the slender veins,  
and at the same time shattering the joints of the bones.

The fountains of the Savior pour forth streams of blood.  
Let the sinner’s soul hurry here;  
let it draw up some of this sacred liquid,  
with which it may frequently anoint the wounds of its sorrow.

### Prayer on the Cross

At last Jesus utters words of charity, sweeter than honey,  
asking forgiveness for the guilty.  
[Col. 0597B] O how abundantly the flood of mercy overflows!  
From now on, let no one despair because of sins.

They crucify and tear you, piling punishment upon punishment,  
but you repay them with grace by praying for them.  
Let no penitent ever lose confidence,  
considering the abundance of saving grace.

### The Conversion of the Good Thief

O admirable mercy of Christ’s goodness!  
From the gallows, calling to you in a sorrowful voice,  
the thief asks forgiveness, and you immediately grant it,  
giving those who repent the hope of forgiveness.

The punishment he endured was demanded by his crime;  
but once he repented at the end of his life,  
he immediately obtained the forgiveness he requested,  
and joyfully received everlasting glory.

### Behold Your Mother

[Col. 0597C]

After this, Jesus looked upon his Mother and summoned her,  
and entrusted her to his beloved disciple.  
He beautifully joined virgin to virgin,  
and from that time the disciple kept her as his mother.

O how grievously the Virgin is inwardly tortured,  
when, deprived of her Son, she is entrusted to another!  
A wondrous exchange is rightly made evident,  
when a servant is exchanged for the Lord in relation to his Mother.

### I Thirst

Speaking again, Jesus said: “I thirst.”  
Immediately someone mixed vinegar with gall  
and offered it to his mouth, poured into a sponge;  
after tasting it a little, he did not wish to drink.

[Col. 0597D] Alas, wondrous Jesus, what were you doing?  
You complained of thirst, but were silent about the cross.  
I think you were not asking for drink chiefly,  
but rather thirsting for our salvation.

### Christ Drained of Blood

The streams of blood had already emptied his veins;  
the appearance of his former beauty fades away.  
A wasting pallor of blood overtakes his face;  
thus the devout power of love triumphs over Jesus.

### Christ Wasting Away

His body is now stretched out, and his throat grows hoarse;  
his lips are contorted, his hair bristles with horror;  
his devout eyes grow faint, and his limbs stiffen;  
the strength of his whole body disappears.

### He Dies

[Col. 0598A]

Uttering his final words, you invoked the Father  
and commended your spirit into his hands.  
At last you expired with a loud cry,  
and thus completed the work of everyone’s salvation.

### The Sun Is Darkened

While the Savior suffers, the heavens are darkened;  
the veil of the Temple is torn, and the tombs are opened;  
the rocks split, and many bodies are raised,  
protesting that the Lord of nature is suffering.

O how deeply night oppressed the Jewish people,  
who, seeing such great miracles, did not believe!  
They impiously rejected and wickedly handed over to death  
the one whom the prophetic voice proclaimed with signs.

### The Virgin’s Lament

[Col. 0598B]

The Virgin of virgins stands beside the Savior’s cross,  
pierced through by the sword of inward sorrow.  
Looking upon the sufferings of her Son and the streams of blood,  
she bears inwardly what he endured outwardly here.

Standing beside her Only-Begotten, the Mother laments;  
alas, she does not know where to turn in her anguish.  
Now she mourns, now she cries aloud, now she adores with groaning,  
yet sorrow does not disfigure her virginal bearing.

With an anxious face the Mother looks upon him hanging there,  
pouring blood abundantly from his wounds.  
She sees the face of her Son pale in death;  
surely sorrow thus tears apart her mind.

Now the dreadful law of nature demands its debt,  
which it formerly withheld from her because of * [an uncertain or corrupt reading] pressure;  
and with interest usury exacts the punishments  
that by common right were owed to mothers.

Again giving birth, you truly experience  
how proper it is for a mother to grieve with her child.  
For bitter groans were wrung from your heart  
by the pains you see your Son enduring.

You are truly pierced through by the sword of sorrow,  
as you see your Son’s long arms stretched out,  
his royal body hanging as though on a balance,  
and his undefiled limbs pouring out blood.

### The Wound in His Side

What mind or tongue, I ask, could tell  
how greatly the Virgin is believed to be tortured within,  
when she sees the side of one already dead wounded  
and the lance searching through the entrails of her Son?

### Blood and Water Flowed Out

[Col. 0598D]

The dead body indeed no longer felt anything;  
but the lance pierced the mother’s breast  
as she saw it fixed in her Son’s side,  
from which the liquid of both water and blood flowed.

Have mercy, Lady, deign to have mercy on the wretched,  
whom Jesus deigns to redeem at so great a price.  
May that very compassion move you to save us;  
contemplate the compassion that compelled you to suffer pains.

Rise, sluggish soul, devoid of vanity.  
Reject the waters of sin; take up healing.  
Behold the purest fountain, the Father of mercy;  
most abundant streams of charity flow forth.

### Devout Exhortation to the Reader

Hasten, then, to this fountain of the Redeemer,  
[Col. 0599A] so that you may draw up some sweetness from its streams;  
from its water, a bath purchased by blood;  
from this source, let healing for your sickness flow.

O wondrous condescension of the merciful Savior!  
O truly marvelous compassion of love!  
You, Jesus, are known to be free from guilt, flower of beauty;  
alas, I am the cause of your suffering.

I am proud—alas!—while you are humbled.  
I commit sins, while you are punished.  
I enjoy sweet things, while you are given gall.  
I seek soft things, while you are treated harshly.

To you, Father, I direct the Propitiator,  
who for my sake poured out his own blood.  
Father, do not despise the sinner, I beg you,  
for whom you know that the Redeemer suffered grievously.

[Col. 0599B] Your sorrowful Passion teaches, Christ,  
how hateful vices are to the Creator,  
how tearful the punishments of hell are,  
and how joyful the joys of heaven are.

From this, diligent reader, you easily understand  
that Jesus suffered to remove our sins,  
to take away the punishments due to us,  
and also to bestow the joys of heaven.

O how admirable a love is demonstrated  
when Jesus is sacrificed for our vices,  
and is crucified for the punishments owed by us,  
purchasing joys through his own sufferings.

Therefore, soul, strive with your strength  
to repay this grace of love worthily.  
Embrace him joyfully with your whole heart;  
desire to love absolutely nothing apart from him.

[Col. 0599C] Jesus, joy of the heart and sweetness of the mind,  
comfort of the soul that trusts in you,  
I earnestly beseech you with devoted prayers:  
mindful of me, be my guardian at every moment.

### The Taking Down of Christ from the Cross

O Jesus, whom the court of heaven venerates,  
how wondrously your work is completed!  
Now it is time for the body to be taken down from the cross,  
and for rest to be granted after this labor.

Afterward Nicodemus and Joseph arrived,  
who had in no way consented to the Lord’s death.  
They drew out the nails from his feet and hands,  
and lifted the body from the gallows.

Now approach quickly, bereaved Mother;  
wipe the pious, bloodied wounds of your Son;  
press blessed kisses upon the wounds;  
gather the sacred offerings of blood.

Who, I ask, could conceive how completely  
the Mother tended the wounds with what devotion,  
how, while tending them, she tried to wipe them with tears,  
and how she kissed them with such frequent kisses?

Now, sweetest Virgin, now the weeping ceases.  
Behold, the Son’s suffering ceases in the tomb,  
and the longed-for day of joy approaches,  
on which he is now to be raised from the dead.

### The Burial of Christ

The Lord’s body is wrapped in a shroud  
and given to burial with spices.  
[Col. 0600A] But lest it be secretly taken away by the disciples,  
the tomb is surrounded by a guard of soldiers.

At last Magdalene kept watch over the place;  
she burned with exceptional love for Jesus.  
She kept vigil as she prepared the aromatic ointments  
with which she hastened to anoint Jesus.

### The Resurrection of Christ

And indeed, at the Lord’s dawn, while these things were being done,  
the Lord rose victorious from the underworld,  
releasing from it the captives whom Limbo held;  
and the tomb appeared empty, with the linens remaining.

A violent earthquake suddenly occurred,  
and an angel descended as the Lord arose.  
Then the vigilant guards, terrified in mind,  
became like dead men under the force of fear.

[Col. 0600B] Afterwards, terrified, they fled from the tomb  
and reported the whole matter to the Jews.  
But the Jews bribed them with a large sum of money  
and instructed them to say that he had been stolen secretly.

O how strange a blindness oppressed the Jews!  
How blind an avarice drove the soldiers!  
Thus truth lay hidden on every side;  
but Jesus did not permit this to continue for long.

### The Woman at the Tomb

At the first light of the Sabbath’s rising dawn,  
Magdalene arrived, burning with love.  
But when she saw the tomb without the Savior,  
she wept, groaned, and cried aloud in anxious grief.

### Woman, Whom Are You Seeking?

[Col. 0600C]

Standing there, the Lord addressed her in an unfamiliar form,  
gently speaking to her as the force of fear was removed:

“Whom are you seeking, devout woman, weeping in this way?  
Do not fear to express the desires of your heart.”

Knower of secrets, who searches hearts,  
why do you ask about the causes of her sorrow?  
Do you lovingly delight in the tears of one who loves,  
whose heart’s desire you approve?

She, Jesus, was seeking absolutely nothing except you;  
with her heart and lips she thirsted only for you.  
For you, forgetful of her sex, she feared no danger;  
for you she groaned anxiously, for you she wept in sorrow.

Thus she thought Jesus was the gardener.  
Yet spiritually she was not greatly mistaken,  
for he was already uprooting the thorns of faithlessness  
and taking care to plant the flowers of faith.

[Col. 0600D] Then the most merciful Savior changed his voice  
and called her by name: “Mary.”  
At this, joyfully following the Lamb, she adored,  
and, adoring, exulted with great joy.

### Christ’s Frequent Appearances

You, sweetest Jesus, after you had risen,  
often made yourself visible to your own.  
At last you ate food with the disciples,  
and, as they watched, you ascended into heaven.

With how much joy, do you think, was the Mother filled  
when she saw her Son, now incapable of suffering,  
rising again? Her grief was immediately erased by joy,  
and a new light arose that would never be taken away.

[Col. 0601A] Now every groan of sorrow is driven away;  
mourning is wondrously changed into gladness.  
While invincible death is defeated and constrained,  
and virtue is restored after vice has been overcome.

But if the disciples rejoice at seeing the Savior,  
with what greater joy, do you think, does his Mother rejoice  
when she sees her reborn Flower,  
whom she had recently seen extinguished in sorrow?

[Col. 0602A] From this point, Virgin, you can safely rejoice;  
from now on sorrow cannot prevail over you,  
nor can death any longer harm your body.  
Therefore, merciful Mother, have mercy on us.

Amen.

[Col. 0601]

## V. OTHER MEDITATIONS: ON THE DEEDS OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, AND ESPECIALLY ON HIS PASSION

### Introduction to the Meditations

[Col. 0601B]

By the swift mercy of Jesus Christ  
and through the intercession of the Virgin Mary,  
I hope that whoever meditates on these words attentively  
will weep with tears out of compassion.

Here are the Apostle’s words, proclaimed to all:  
“Those who are gathered together [perhaps: ‘those who reign together’] are those who suffer together;  
those who compete lawfully will be crowned,  
and those who judge themselves will not be judged.”

Therefore it is fitting for us to ponder Christ’s wounds,  
to love them inwardly with compassionate weeping,  
to overcome our enemies with God’s help,  
and, having exposed our sins, to expiate them with tears.

Therefore, whoever you are who reads what follows, deign  
[Col. 0601C] to gather together the powers of your affections.  
Strive to drive vanities far from your mind,  
and, while reading, do not hurry in a merely superficial way.

If you wish to think more often of Jesus in these passages,  
you need not always recite the whole work.  
Read wherever you can more quickly rouse yourself  
and more sweetly nourish your devout spirit.

Thus, reader, while reading, hold your mind  
as though you were gazing upon Jesus as a nursing child,  
growing into a young man through each successive age;  
likewise, see the Virgin serving him.

See him revealing miracles and suffering death,  
and her almost everywhere and always imitating him,  
bitterly mourning the sufferings of her Son,  
and inwardly enduring each of his torments.

[Col. 0601D] Although the page does not seem clearly  
to express the measure of the Virgin’s sorrow,  
it is nevertheless fitting for us to ponder it from this,  
and to turn it over eagerly in our hearts again and again.

### Lament over Human Ignorance

O most wretched human being, remember what you are,  
and always remember for what purpose you were made.  
Reflect upon how God made you, wretched one.  
Alas, you cannot consider what you have made of yourself!

He who created all things made you sufficiently good,  
and he often restored you after sin had cast you down.  
Alas, alas, why are you ungrateful to him who washed you  
with his holy blood, which he shed drop by drop for you?

O wicked, most vain, envious, pompous one,  
[Col. 0602B] angry, greedy, fornicating, gluttonous,  
lying, lazy, negligent, slanderous, deceitful,  
you are the servant of every evil, excessively vicious.

Come to your senses, most wicked one, while God calls you,  
lest on the day of judgment you be punished as guilty.  
Do not remain ungrateful like the false Judas;  
but cry out very often: “Spare me, my God.”

Be ashamed, impious and ungrateful soul.  
Alas, why do you not reflect? Why are you hardened?  
Let out sighs with weeping and groan prostrate,  
so that the Almighty may erase your sins.

Alas, how great is the dullness of the soul!  
How often disgrace occupies it in various ways,  
in which there is no habit of holiness,  
[Col. 0602C] unless perhaps scarcely even a feigned resemblance!

Rarely does it see its own conduct or scarcely remember it;  
scarcely can the wretched soul rouse itself to pray.  
It desires to read more than to pray,  
but, alas, it cannot be satisfied with vanities.

For while praying, it entreats the Most High,  
it often meditates on almost useless things.  
Alas, it does not even remember that it is guilty,  
but wanders aimlessly, roaming everywhere.

It strives to appear outwardly like a lamb,  
but inwardly, alas, it remains like a fox.  
While it performs the services owed to God,  
it is always turning about like a millstone.

O how often it turns its face away from you  
and quickly turns toward harmful concerns!
[Col. 0602D]  
It pays no attention to what it ought to do,  
but, occupying itself wrongly, corrupts itself.

Indeed, the lips of the flesh sing words of life,  
and the body has often rightly adored something;  
but this is the evil of a soul that has forgotten God,  
stripped of virtues and worn down by vices.

O madness of the heart, greatly to be abhorred,  
justly to be punished severely by the Lord!  
O wandering of the heart, continually to be lamented  
and, with the Lord’s help, to be mourned by all!

O emptiness of the heart, O restlessness!  
Alas, alas, this is the sickness of my soul,  
from which true holiness has withdrawn,  
as has perfect repentance for its own crime.

[Col. 0603A] My God, heal me with your medicine,  
me, deserving the twofold death of body and soul.  
Quickly offer me the cup of salvation,  
and, I beg you, hasten to help me.

Spare me, one Trinity and triune Unity,  
Father, Son, Spirit, divine Majesty.  
Spare me, you who created me, lest the serpent’s deceit  
crush me, your believer, in the ruin of death.

Father, through your Son, the Messiah, I beg you:  
make me love you alone, and make me know myself.  
Let me continually contemplate his precious Passion;  
let me become humble in the eyes of my heart.

For the sake of the Virgin Mother I ask you, good Jesus,  
to wound my heart with your Passion,  
so that from it I may continually enjoy meditation,  
and compassion for the Virgin Mary.

Holy Spirit of God, who in the Godhead  
and are [the] third Person, full of mercy:  
I beg you, always grant yourself to me as propitious,  
and make me mindful of Christ’s gracious Passion.

### God’s Benefits

My God, how much I owe to this mercy,  
that you formed me in your image;  
you who were willing to make a vile little worm of me—  
O how many gifts you have increased up to this time!

You cleansed me, born in sins, through baptism;  
you have always supplied the necessities of food;  
you gave me form, abundance of possessions, and honors,  
and now placed me in an excellent position.

[Note: [Col. 0603D] Anselm appears here to be speaking of his monastic life. See the legend and commentary, nos. 25 and 26.]

### Human Ingratitude

[Col. 0603C] Alas, I know that I am ungrateful for all these gifts,  
because I do not keep the Lord’s commandment,  
but render a most negligent service;  
and I am excessively inclined toward every sin.

O sorrow, O groaning! What have I done?  
[Note: [Col. 0603D] He appears to lament the investiture in a bishopric received from Henry. See there, [Col. 0604D].]  
Into what great perversity have I thrown myself?  
There is no evil that I have not done;  
alas, among all good things there is nothing I have completed.

Alas, what will a soul do when thus cast down in evils,  
a soul that stinks in vices like one rejected?  
Certainly here she must be sought as an Advocate,  
who has often proved herself a refuge for the guilty.

### Supplication to the Virgin Mary

O Mother and Queen of mercy,  
[Col. 0603D] ever remaining Virgin, divine Mother,  
have mercy on the soul that lies face upward,  
oppressed by the sewer of manifold sin.

I beseech you, for God’s sake, through whom life came,  
whose clemency is everywhere present,  
through whom the devil’s cunning has been crushed,  
so that through you the justice of your Son may be softened.

First, make me love the Lord perfectly;  
let me never abandon him in meditation, nor you.  
Let me always live rightly in the Catholic faith,  
free from every scandal of an unbelieving sect.

[Col. 0604D] The Henricians and schismatics are indicated. See there, nos. 86 and 87.]

O how great are the graces that through you  
[Col. 0604A] the once-lost human being received, whom the devil deceived,  
when the Most High assumed human nature from you  
and mercifully began to help us.

### Rebuke of Human Ignorance

The highest Majesty emptied itself  
and clothed itself in pure flesh through you.  
When the course of nine months was completed, it came forth—  
a speechless little child, who lives immeasurably.

Behold how greatly the Almighty bends down for you;  
and still, foul man, your heart swells with pride?  
God, the Son of God, weeps for you,  
and still your heart rejoices in laughter?

### Christ’s Nativity

God is born poor, and you wish to grow rich?  
He is placed in a manger, and you wish to be honored?  
[Col. 0604B] O stinking pride, learn not to act foolishly,  
because he himself commanded us to imitate him.

He is needy and is born in the cold on the road.  
Mary nurses, bathes, and feeds him.  
Here he teaches us, devoutly, not to reject hardship,  
while Christ, the noble child, weeps, thirsts, and hungers.

Most devout infant, have mercy on me.  
I ask this for the sake of your Mother’s sincere service:  
give me tears of true charity,  
so that I may grieve with your sufferings.

### Circumcision

Alas, why do I not share in his suffering by rejecting laughter  
and washing my eyes with bitter tears,  
while the tenderest child suffers circumcision—  
the child whom Paradise praises with the choir of heaven?

### The Adoration of the Magi

[Col. 0604C]

The angels announced you to the shepherds,  
and the Magi adored you with gifts.  
Soon the treacherous plotted to destroy you,  
but your parents fled from their homeland with you.

### Flight into Egypt

Who would not grieve with so small an infant  
who so quickly began to suffer ambushes,  
enduring the labors of this journey,  
while the Virgin Mother carried him?

For the Mother, who scarcely used to leave the house,  
was now compelled by the danger threatening her Son  
to flee from her homeland by night  
with the newborn child whom she carried with her.

[Col. 0604D] O most devout Jesus, O tender child,  
for the love of the maiden Mary I beg you:  
fill me with the gall of all your Passion,  
and compel me continually to serve you.

O fruitful Branch, O flower among women,  
Lady of angels and of the whole world,  
I beg you, reveal to me whatever was bitter  
among all that you endured for the salvation of souls.

Would that I had then been Joseph’s little servant!  
Certainly I would most willingly have carried you, Jesus,  
or at least led the Virgin’s donkey,  
and joyfully fulfilled every service.

[Col. 0605A] I would have gathered apples, roses, and lilies,  
and whatever might have pleased the little boy.  
Alas, why was it not permitted me to see you  
and do these things for the most beautiful little child?

Perhaps, devout little one, you would not have rejected me,  
but would have graciously accepted my service,  
mercifully smiled upon your attentive servant,  
and granted forgiveness to one who asked.

### Disputation in the Temple

While the twelve-year-old boy remains  
in the Temple of Jerusalem, the Mother is saddened.  
When she finds him, she marvels with Joseph,  
as he questions the learned and speaks astonishing things.

O who knows the groans of the grieving Virgin,  
who sought her only-begotten Son for three days,  
and lovingly complained about why he had done this?  
With this sorrow, wound the heart of the reader, Jesus.

“O how often,” I imagine Christ’s Mother saying,  
“alas, my comfort, why have you left me?  
Where, my only Son, alas, where have you gone?  
Return, I beg you, my son; return to your sorrowful mother.”

Would that my heart languished after Jesus in this way  
and suffered inwardly while continually seeking him!  
Perhaps the most merciful one would appear to me  
and offer me firm hope in his mercy.

But alas, Jesus, my heart lacks this languor.  
For rarely does it seek you, and then not fervently.  
Draw it back to yourself, my Jesus, with fear;  
bind it with love in tranquil sweetness.

You submit to your parents, while ruling all things;  
all things serve you, yet you in turn serve them.  
O divine charity, you are spread abroad exceedingly,  
while for us wretched people you endure adversity.

### Baptism

You are baptized and proclaimed by the Father’s voice,  
while a heavenly dove descends upon you.  
In the desert you hunger, O eternal Power;  
having conquered the enemy, you gather brotherly hosts.

### Water Made Wine

Invited to a wedding, you began your signs,  
at the urging of your Mother, who is kindly toward all.  
O why is such a worthy Mother reproved,  
who refuses no one the signs of her compassion?

Yet you immediately did what she had suggested,  
because nothing could happen except what you willed.  
For you changed water into the finest wine,  
and through this led the disciples to faith.

O most pure Virgin, full of the highest good,  
you enrich all the wretched with your sacred gifts.  
Fill us with the finest wine of devotion;  
give us one stream of compunction.

Alas, most kind and blessed Mother,  
in us devotion is nothing but pretense.  
Our hearts are cold and our souls afflicted;  
come quickly to the wretched, renowned hope of the guilty.

Most kind Jesus, for the honor of your Mother,  
turn our cold hearts toward your love.  
So that we may always ponder the great labor  
and the great suffering that you endured for us.

[Col. 0606A] For by giving us an example in your practices,  
you fulfill by spending the night in prayer  
what you teach us to do;  
in keeping vigil, you grow weary, hungry, and thirsty through labor.

### Miracles

You travel through villages and fortresses, preaching the kingdom;  
healing the deaf, mute, sick, and blind;  
driving out demons, raising the dead;  
and, by forgiving sins, you grant pardon to many.

You are also said to have grown weary while disputing,  
often reproved by the Jews themselves,  
many times insulted by them,  
and at times even blasphemed by them.

For me, how much you endure, O blessedness!  
For me you become as one weak, O strength of God.  
For me you appear vile, O true beauty;  
you become as one in need, O supreme fullness.

For me you are narrowed, O vast breadth;  
for me you are shortened, O expansive length;  
for me you are bent down, O great height;  
for me you stoop forward, O lofty magnitude.

Why do you endure so many hardships, O such sublime greatness?  
Your righteousness is altogether upright.  
Therefore let the multitude of so many gifts overcome me,  
so that gratitude toward you may always be in me.

### The Triumph at Jerusalem

When the time of preaching had been completed,  
why do you thus hasten to Jerusalem upon a donkey,  
you who sit upon thrones, for the sake of your Passion?  
The crowds resound with a voice of veneration.

[Col. 0606C] Now hurry, soul; run without delay,  
because, as you consider, behold, the hour is coming.  
Adore the Lord, praising him with the others,  
and beg that he lead you with him to the cross.

O how greatly the Mother and friends rejoiced,  
seeing Jesus blessed by the people,  
and hearing “Hosanna” said to Christ, Son of David!  
But alas, his enemies were envious of this.

O my confidence, blessed Mother,  
rejoicing greatly in the praise of your Son,  
alas, with how much sorrow will you be tortured shortly,  
when you see all these things changed?

### Christ Is Sold

For the chief rulers, transgressors of the law,  
take counsel for the death of the Son;  
having fixed a price, the worst of buyers  
allow themselves to become debtors to Judas.

Alas, alas, my Lady, singular Virgin!  
Your Son has been sold, and are you still rejoicing?  
Alas, why do you not openly beg your only-begotten Son  
that you yourself might die before he suffers?

You take great delight in your Son’s presence  
and imitate him with the greatest affection.  
Alas, you reflect less upon your soul,  
which is soon to be tortured by bitter grief.

Alas, how long do I remain sluggish in a heart so hard,  
feeling no compassion for Jesus who is about to die,  
or for the great sorrow that soon afterward  
will almost destroy my sweet Lady?

[Col. 0607A] Jesus, from whom absolutely nothing is hidden,  
how long will you tolerate foolish Judas with you?  
While he offers you a feigned devotion,  
he greatly longs for the time when he will betray you.

Then, having sent the disciples with the sign of a water jar,  
you go to the lodging prepared for the supper.  
Then you sit in the midst of the twelvefold crowd  
and command them serenely to love one another.

### He Eats the Supper

Then, as you had foretold, you say that you will die  
and that one of them will betray you.  
You say that each of them will flee from you,  
and that Peter will deny you three times this very night.

O sorrow, O groaning! How greatly they were troubled!  
They all grieved over so great a crime,  
[Col. 0607B] when they promised that they would not flee.  
And immediately they asked who the betrayer would be.

### He Washes the Feet

Meanwhile you give an example of humility,  
washing the feet of your subjects yourself.  
You also freely give your own body as food  
to them and to all baptized into you.

### He Institutes the Eucharist

O what shall I do, mass of sins,  
most wretched of all the wretched,  
while you bend your knees, King of the universe,  
and wash the feet of your servants?

Most merciful Jesus, fountain of pure love,  
you loved mortal human beings so greatly  
that you gave yourself as food to believers,  
[Col. 0607C] and commanded them to receive you in remembrance of you.

Most kind Christ, Son of the highest God,  
I, most unworthy, beg you to have mercy on me.  
Give me so much charity, faith, and hope  
that I may worthily receive the mystery of so great a reality.

What thanks shall I return for your enriching me in this way?  
For assigning me to so great a mystery?  
For continually tolerating me, unworthy and wretched,  
and allowing me to remain with your servants?

Alas, what shall I do, O supreme sweetness?  
Why am I so undevout while I eat you yourself?  
Alas, I approach excessively guilty and hard;  
alas, I am hard there, and hard when I depart.

O Jesus, what shall I do, a worm and corruption?  
The blackness of sin oppresses my mind.  
[Col. 0607D]  
Make me a worthy minister, O God in whom I believe;  
for the love of the Virgin Mother I intercede.

It is most certainly astonishing that, by eating you,  
the soul does not melt in pure love.  
But alas, I hunger and repay you with hardness,  
and I cannot be softened even a little by weeping.

Spare me, merciful Lord, by granting  
that I may continually be moved to compunction as I receive you,  
always honoring the Virgin Mother and you,  
and recalling your Last Supper in my mind.

O if my Lady had then been present  
and had heard that her Son was to be betrayed that night,  
she certainly would not have eaten any food,  
but would immediately have given herself to bitter tears.

[Col. 0608A] Alas for me, my dearest, my beloved,  
praise of all the saints, never once guilty!  
Would that you were now in Galilee,  
so that you would not see your Son suffering in Judea!

Devout Jesus, I beg you, for love of your Mother,  
fill me now with the weight of your deepest sorrow,  
so that, grieving with you in the greatest fervor,  
I may roar with sighs and abundant weeping.

Let me see with the eyes of my heart, as though present,  
you enduring each suffering for me,  
your Mother grieving with you beside you,  
as though dying amid each of the torments.

Virgin Mother of God, blessed above all,  
[Col. 0608B] I beg you by the mercy born from you:  
reveal to me how you were burdened,  
so greatly tortured by your child before your eyes.

My Lady, my Lady, full of graces,  
I beg you, give me your bitter heart,  
and most abundant streams of tears,  
so that I may feel the force of your anguish.

Would that, by your gift, Jesus Christ,  
this sorrow might torture me greatly every day,  
as it tortured the sad heart of the Virgin Mother  
when cruel torturers crucified you!

God-man, who could think attentively about you,  
remaining in a body so capable of suffering,  
having suffered so many anguishes in body and mind,  
and not suddenly dissolve entirely into tears?

Who, O Mother of God, could meditate  
[Col. 0608C] upon you weeping while your Son is tortured by punishments,  
and already wearied by such great anguish,  
and not immediately be changed into weeping?

Alas for me, most hard-hearted one! Why do I not weep with you?  
Alas, why am I so hard while I beseech you, Mother?  
Lady surrounded by the choir of the heavenly powers,  
give me abundant tears, I implore you.

### He Prays in the Garden

Hear Jesus, soul, as though he were now present,  
saying to the disciples, “Rise, let us go from here,”  
and respond quickly, entreating as he speaks:  
“Make me, Jesus, follow you as you go toward death.”

### He Sweats Blood

See him urging the disciples to pray,  
and, while praying, falling three times to the ground before the Father;  
his flesh troubled, sorrowful, and fearful,  
[Col. 0608D]  
and sweat of blood flowing from him.

What are you doing, most valiant Son of the living God?  
Are you so sorrowful that these streams flow?  
I have never heard of such great anguish,  
and yet, alas, I was unable to weep as I ought.

What if my Lady had seen this while present?  
Would she have fallen asleep with the apostles?  
Certainly not; she would have wept greatly  
and almost fainted from excessive grief.

Alas, alas, my Lady, ever-pure Virgin,  
the hour is already near; tomorrow is the coming day,  
when you will see your only-begotten Son  
failing on the cross in death of greatest hardship.

But now see, soul, the malignant crowd  
[Col. 0609A] and the most treacherous Judas kissing Jesus.  
Hear Jesus ask what Judas had come for,  
and call that most wicked man “friend.”

Then, when the Lord says to them in the gentlest voice,  
“Whom are you seeking?” they suddenly fall down.  
What will they do then when Jesus comes  
as a terrible Judge appearing to them?

O who can think without a groan  
of those most impious men binding you, Jesus,  
and so harshly tightening your most holy hands?  
Alas, why can I, most wicked one, not weep?

### He Is Led to Annas

Then all the disciples flee in fear,  
alas, leaving you alone among the savage men.  
They are certainly exceedingly hard-hearted, if, seeing  
[Col. 0609B] you led to Annas, they are not grieving.

### The Disciples Flee

O holy disciples, O my patrons!  
Why do you not show faithfulness to your pledge?  
Yet the word of the good Master is most true,  
when you are so inclined to hurried flight.

Nevertheless, I understand that you grieve greatly  
and are inwardly tormented in your minds.  
But I ask you to deign to pray to Jesus  
that he give me a heart’s bitter sadness.

### He Is Cruelly Treated

O most holy Virgin, if you had been present  
and had seen your Son bound so tightly by the impious,  
and treated by them contemptuously,  
you would truly have uttered a most bitter lament.

### He Is Struck on the Cheek

[Col. 0609C]

Do you not reflect on how Jesus is being treated—  
seized by evil men and injured by bonds?  
Alas, why does my spirit remain untouched  
while Christ is struck on the cheek before Annas?

How long, most merciful Lady, do you delay wounding  
my heart with the anguish of your dear Son?  
O my confidence, I beg you, deign  
to grant that I may suffer his sorrows and wounds!

Contemplate, soul, Jesus abandoned  
and held tightly in harsh bonds,  
sentenced in the wicked council of the rulers,  
and, like a simple lamb, saying nothing.

### He Is Sent to Caiaphas

Confess, while venerating him, that he was falsely accused,  
[Col. 0609D] mocked by Caiaphas and interrogated;  
but understand well that Jesus was again rejected  
and appointed to be the future Judge.

Most kind Christ, who will come  
on the last day to judge us,  
delightful to the just, whom you will save,  
terrible to the unjust, whom you will condemn,  
I beg you, most devout Lord, by the worthy blood  
that you shed for me upon the wood of the cross:  
then show me your gracious face,  
so that I may fear no evil spirit.

For the sake of the Virgin Mother, who at your right hand  
will then sit nobly, to pray for her own,  
save me forever with your saints,  
upon whom you now rain, both upon the impious and the devout.

[Col. 0610A] O who can meditate without tears  
on the fact that you, Jesus, allowed yourself to be so afflicted,  
judged a blasphemer by Caiaphas,  
and condemned by the wicked to a most shameful death?

### He Is Mocked and Spat Upon

After this, almost everyone rushes upon you,  
shamefully spitting upon your splendid face,  
striking you everywhere with slaps and blows,  
rousing the minds of those who love you to mourning.

Look sorrowfully, soul, at these savages,  
tearing out the hair of your head and beard,  
striking your veiled face with their hands,  
and doing every kind of evil they could.

### Soliloquies

O sorrow, O groaning! Why do I, wretched man,  
[Col. 0610B] not grieve inwardly while reading these evils?  
Only because I am evil and conceal this very fact,  
and, alas, sometimes deny that I am so.

Delicate face of God, Jesus Christ,  
look upon me with those eyes with which you looked upon Peter  
when he denied you three times, as you had foretold,  
so that I may grieve with you, so sad for my own sake.

O impious, proud, and vain Jews,  
why do you rage in this way, like madmen?  
He is God, the Son of God, O utterly profane men,  
whom you afflict in such an inhuman manner.

Most powerful Jesus, Son of the true God,  
why do you wish to appear so vile for the wretched?  
Certainly you are full of sincere love,  
[Col. 0610C]  
since you wish to be tortured so greatly by impious men.

O if my Lady saw you standing there  
and devoutly enduring such great anguish,  
no one, I think, ever saw her weeping like this,  
as one would see her, wishing to suffer as well.

Alas, what will you do, worthy Majesty,  
Mary, who nourished him, supreme Power,  
tomorrow when you see him fall into hostile hands,  
and the powers of his body dry up like potsherds?

O my confidence, if you saw your beloved Son—
You would see him subjected to many insults and punishments,  
blasphemed while raised upon the cross,  
and you would say that he was exceedingly upright.

Alas! alas! my Lady, what grief you will suffer  
a little later, when you see the fruit of your womb  
[Col. 0610D] led by the wicked to dreadful torments  
and, tortured, wasting away as though already destroyed?

O Jesus, who are God and perfect man,  
why do you wish to sit so contemptuously in such vile humiliation,  
alas, for us wretched beings to be so subjected,  
mocked and utterly despised for our sake?

Seeing the Lord undergo unworthy things for his sake,  
what believer would dare to seek  
or boast any longer about his own gifts,  
rather than, spurning everything, follow after Christ?

Indeed, it is fitting for each person who wishes to be saved  
always to contemplate his own wretchedness,  
not to rejoice vainly in the praise of his tongue,  
but, piously, to imitate the despised Lord.

[Col. 0611A] Therefore, let it be far from us to think highly of ourselves;  
let it be sweet to hear words of reproach;  
with a pious heart let us continually give anger its place;  
let us strive to obey everyone well.

Alas for me, most wicked, who love to be praised,  
who, although guilty, refuse to be blamed,  
and often presume to call myself praiseworthy;  
alas for me—who can be compared with one so evil?

O most merciful Jesus, who are the true vine,  
cherish me as a branch and make me gentle;  
let me have a persevering thirst for righteousness;  
I pray that I may never be the author of conflict, but its peacemaker.

Mother of God, I beseech your compassion:  
grant me the truest humility;  
drive out envy and harshness,  
and obtain for me perfect charity.

[Col. 0611B] O my confidence, Mother of the Creator,  
now I offer myself to you, nurse of the Redeemer;  
help me, I pray, guiding me at every hour;  
make me mindful of the sorrow of your sword.

Although no one, Lady, can fully express  
the sorrows you endured at the death of your beloved Son,  
nevertheless it is fitting for us often to meditate upon them  
and, weeping, to grieve inwardly with you.

Therefore, most holy Lady, I beg you, deign  
to place some true understanding of this in my heart,  
and enable me to mark it down by writing in such a way  
that it may stir those who love you.

Jesus Is Brought before Pilate

But now behold, O soul, those who envy him:  
[Col. 0611C] the leaders of the Jews, raging against Christ,  
dragging him bound mockingly through the streets,  
and bringing him before the governor Pilate.

O Jesus, who were wickedly bound for me,  
accused for me by false testimony,  
and also counted among thieves for me,  
grant me tears, so that I may grieve with you.

I beg you, make me a messenger to my Lady-Savior,  
the most holy Virgin, your Mother,  
so that she may come at once, together with her friends,  
and see what your enemies are doing to you.

Hasten now, O soul, though unwillingly,  
to announce these things to the Lady, and do so reverently;  
act both cautiously and wisely,  
lest she receive this news impatiently.

[Col. 0611D] Now speak as though she were present, in a sorrowful voice:

Praise to you, mother who gave birth, beautiful Virgin;  
I beg you, most holy and gracious Mother,  
let what I report to you  
not be burdensome.

You know well, Lady, that the Almighty  
was made flesh in you and was born in the world,  
and lived for a long time among sinners,  
having become human for our sake in order to redeem us.

Therefore, as far as you are able, do not be disturbed,  
lest you cause your Son to suffer more on your account;  
but deign to ask him for one thing:  
that he grant me to grieve greatly for his sake.

And if she should ask: “What sorrowful news do you have?”  
you should say: “Come, Lady, if you wish to see  
your Son Jesus, or speak with him,  
who is beginning to be offered to the Father for us.”

[Col. 0612A] Then, understanding that her beloved Son had been seized  
and finally led in chains to Pilate,  
she immediately broke into the bitterest weeping,  
and collapsed prostrate upon the ground.

But compelled by love for her dearest Son,  
she rose as quickly as possible, suffused with pallor,  
and hurried to the Son, overcome with grief,  
restraining her cry with virginal modesty.

Then the Lady’s sisters, helping her,  
went more swiftly to Jesus whom they loved,  
showing by their tears the sorrows of their hearts;  
but Mary Magdalene shed still greater tears.

“Ladies, consider carefully what you are doing.  
[Col. 0612B] I beg you, be silent from weeping for a little while;  
wipe away your tears, or remain here,  
lest by weeping indiscreetly you torment Jesus.”

But when they came quickly to the Lord,  
and looked upon him amid such disgrace,  
grieving with still greater and more abundant tears,  
they moved all who loved him to sorrow.

Then, when the Lady saw her only Son  
more afflicted than any thief,  
her heart was troubled beyond expression,  
and thus, as though dead, she scarcely retained her breath.

But Jesus was more troubled on account of the Virgin,  
and grieved for her more than for his own sufferings.

Alas! alas! Jesus, you are tormented on every side;  
within and without you are burdened exceedingly.

[Col. 0612C] Alas! no one ever knew such great sorrow,  
nor did anyone hear such grievous groans;  
and this is not surprising, for he who always lives  
underwent manifold suffering there.

Contemplate Jesus carefully, O soul,  
placed so irreverently among the wicked.  
When the governor Pilate repeatedly questioned him,  
he marveled at his silence, utterly astonished.

Jesus, who could not speak falsehood  
and yet remained silent, keeping truth unspoken,  
do not let me fall through talkativeness,  
but grant me discerning silence.

O Jesus, give me a heart instructed to ponder  
the Virgin’s weeping and lamentation,  
as she hastens after you, led to Herod,  
[Col. 0612D] and despised in a white garment, then brought back.

O Virgin, whom a storm of sorrows overwhelms,  
where did you receive, Lady, such strength  
that you could follow these criminal people?  
Truly, the love of your Son conquered grievous circumstances.

O my confidence, who have no equal,  
I would gladly walk with you,  
and willingly support you, weakened by weeping,  
or, if only you would give me tears, weep with you.

Who could meditate without a groan  
upon Jesus being treated so shamefully and badly,  
perhaps having his feet injured by the hurried journey?  
For he was not accustomed to wearing shoes.

Behold, the bitterest things that follow are taking place,  
[Col. 0613A] and what is now inflicted is rightly worthy of compassion.  
Therefore people are rightly called ungrateful  
when they so often fail to grieve with Jesus.

Now prepare yourself, devout soul,  
to grieve over Jesus, offering him your vows;  
multiply your tears, and be piously washed by them;  
if you can, melt entirely for him.

Behold how exceedingly dearly Christ loves you:  
he wishes to save you by his blood,  
and thus free you by the most shameful death—  
yet you always neglect him and do not wish to love him in return.

O most merciful Jesus, come to the aid of me who ask,  
who until now have neglected to love you,  
and, what is much worse, have often been unwilling to do so,  
alas, offending you frequently by despising you.

Most merciful one, forgive me as I confess;  
save and help me, who seek you yourself.  
Come to meet me, your prodigal son returning late,  
and spare me, my Father, as I make this request.

Jesus, who are filled with compassion,  
be willing to wound me with your Passion,  
so that I may grieve with you out of love,  
as I now behold you in affliction.

Who can see without a groan those wicked men  
stripping you, Jesus, without reverence,  
binding you wickedly to the column,  
and scourging your body with terrible violence?

Jesus Is Scourged

Trembling, behold, O soul, the seated executioners,  
tearing this tender flesh with whips,  
[Col. 0613C]  
inflicting wounds upon your wounds,  
and piling bruises upon bruises.

Who would not mourn, seeing the ruler of the world  
drenched in blood as though he were unclean,  
this most holy body trembling all over,  
and the most compassionate breast wholly groaning?

Contemplate, O soul, his shins and arms,  
filled everywhere with innumerable blows,  
all the limbs of his body covered with blood,  
and open streams of gore flowing down.

O most holy body, fastened to the column,  
afflicted for me with the bitterest scourges,  
clothed all around in rosy blood,  
take away from me, I beg you, every sin.

[Col. 0613D] Most holy soul, so burdened for me,  
afflicted for me by the greatest pains,  
I beseech you, through the Virgin who grieved over you,  
continually wash away all my sins.

But Mary, the Mother, afflicting herself,  
continually multiplies her tears by weeping;  
she utters deep sighs, groaning bitterly,  
and crushes her breast with sorrowful sobs.

Who could see you, O Mother,  
mourning inconsolably, without a groan?  
Give me tears; make me weep with you.  
I beseech you, O my hope, have mercy on me.

Behold, her modest eyes swell from weeping;  
her most radiant cheeks grow pale everywhere;  
but, alas, the Son’s limbs redden with blood,  
[Col. 0614A] and your anguish gathers ever more intensely.

After the malicious scourging,  
so deeply grievous to all who love him,  
another grave and shameful outrage immediately follows,  
one far more insulting:

He Is Mocked

For, gathering the entire cohort of soldiers,  
they surround gentle Jesus, mocking him with insults,  
shamefully stripping him again,  
and clothing him in a purple garment.

He Is Crowned with Thorns

Then plaiting a painful crown of thorns  
and pressing it deeply onto Jesus’ head,  
they place a reed in his right hand as a scepter,  
and, kneeling, cry “Hail!” in mockery.

[Col. 0614B] Mourning, behold, O soul, the executioners striking him,  
spitting upon the Lord’s most beautiful face,  
violently beating his head with the reed.  
O, why does this pain not torment our minds?

O Lord’s head, worthy of veneration by all,  
you are bloodied and pierced, dreaded by the angels;  
you are beaten and spat upon, revered by the saints;  
truly, devout souls ought to grieve for you inwardly.

O splendid face, afflicted by blows,  
alas, you are wholly painted with spit and blood,  
now seemingly abandoned by God to his enemies.  
Alas for the sorrow! My sins do all this.

Good, good Lord, why do you permit yourself  
to be tortured by such harsh pains for us impure beings?  
Spare yourself these sufferings, Lord—spare them, or those to come;  
[Col. 0614C] spare yourself, I beg you, or spare your Mother’s anguish.

Meanwhile, the most wicked Pilate came out  
and urged the people not to kill Jesus;  
for no guilt had been found in him,  
but the perverse crowd spoke against him.

Pilate’s and the People’s Opposing Voices

Then he brought out God, bloodied by scourging,  
and said: “Take him, corrected.”  
But, full of deceit, they denied the man presented to them,  
demanding from the judge the criminal.

The judge continued striving not to do this,  
but the people shouted in opposition: “Crucify him!”  
Then the unjust man sentenced the Lord to death,  
and the most wicked crowd rejoiced at this.

Although these things were foretold with horror,  
[Col. 0614D] they are small when compared with what follows.

Alas, how greatly the Mother was afflicted by these things!  
As I judge, she was almost lifeless.

Contemplate, O soul, how burdensome it is  
for a mother to see her Son’s head crowned with thorns,  
to see him, more beautiful in form than all the sons of men,  
now more horrible than a leper.

Alas, how burdened you are, Queen of heaven,  
seeing your Son crowned with thorns!  
Certainly sudden pain has rushed upon you;  
from it, I beg you, hasten to wound me.

Then holy Magdalene and all the friends  
groan most bitterly in unhappy grief;  
I think this sorrow cannot be expressed in words,  
[Col. 0615A] but Christ’s enemies consider it of little account.

Christ Is Given the Cross

At once the perverse soldiers take up the cross,  
place it upon the Lord’s shoulder,  
and lead Jesus mockingly through Jerusalem,  
displaying the disgrace of the cross to everyone.

Now attend, O soul, to Jesus, exceedingly gracious,  
burdened for you by the weight of the wood of the cross.  
Know that his tender shoulder is wounded,  
and that Jesus is mocked by the wicked people.

The Crowd Follows the Bearer

Alas, Jesus, I consider something exceedingly grievous:  
the hostile crowd of soldiers close around you,  
then the especially wicked Jews,  
and your friends, far away, grieving beyond measure.

[Col. 0615B] Alas, such a procession is not worthy of praise,  
for its first part is wholly raging,  
its second is worse, as though frenzied,  
and, alas, its third is wholly groaning for you!

The Mother and the Pious Women

Seeing these things, Christ’s Mother, trembling with grief,  
rushes into sorrow as one who is dying.  
Who, thinking about this, would not weep from anguish?  
Certainly he is exceedingly hard-hearted or devoid of love!

But the Lady’s sisters support her  
and walk behind the Lord, grieving intensely;  
everywhere they see people pursuing Jesus  
and loudly shouting that he is a criminal.

Christ Forbids Weeping

Then the Lord turned and began to forbid  
the daughters of Jerusalem to mourn over him,  
but told them to weep over themselves and over their children,  
foretelling that those who had not borne children would be blessed.

Who could meditate without a groan  
upon you, Virgin who gave birth, being so distressed?  
Upon all who love you shedding so many tears,  
and Jesus being treated thus on the way to Calvary?

O Mother, why do you hasten with Jesus to the cross?  
Do you wish to suffer a cruel death with your Son?  
Alas, where will you see the leader of Judea die,  
he who created the cherubim above the true light?

Virgin, who promptly help those who pray to you,  
make me quickly grieve with compassion for Christ’s sufferings;  
give me tears abundantly now, I beg you,  
and make me persevere in contemplating him.

He Is Given Vinegar to Drink

[Col. 0615D]

Alas for the sorrow, and for this grievous change!  
For the Lord Messiah is given vinegar to drink.  
Alas, the cross is immediately prepared so that he may undergo death,  
and he is stripped for the third time with great violence.

Unless you have a heart of stone, scarcely possessing fear,  
pay close attention, and you will have tears;  
consider this garment removed from Jesus,  
whom you should know already to be covered with wounds from the scourging.

He Is Stripped of His Garments

Behold the most wicked crowd pulling at this garment,  
which clings forcefully everywhere to skin and flesh;  
look at the blood flowing from the reopened wounds,  
and at Jesus suffering grievously from this injury.

[Col. 0616A] Certainly the great severity of this torment  
would be sufficient to move any attentive person to tears.  
Alas for me, who grieve too little, though so hard-hearted;  
merciful Jesus, give me the tears I ask for.

Virgin, like whom none has ever been found,  
can you still live while seeing these torments?  
Behold, your Son’s naked limbs are bloodied;  
alas, you are still kept alive to see such things.

Considering you, Virgin, weeping anxiously,  
I grieve for you, Lady, but alas, not bitterly.  
Most merciful Lady, I beg you, deign  
to wound me with this pain of yours.

You see, my Lady, your noble Son,  
whom the Prophet calls more beautiful than all others,  
now a man of sorrows under pressing pains,  
[Col. 0616B] and, alas, wholly ulcerated by many wounds.

O Jewish crowd, faithless and obscene,  
O harsh poisons of your hardness,  
O most wicked people, full of every evil,  
why are you moved by nothing in such harsh suffering?

So, my soul, hard and perverse,  
why are you not turned to weeping by this torment?  
Why are you not sprinkled with bitter tears,  
seeing the Lord’s limbs covered with blood?

O Jesus, deign to help me immediately;  
make me taste your bitterness.  
Make me weep for your sufferings,  
for I am ashamed to contemplate this without tears.

Alas, this is truly pitiable and astonishing:  
whoever contemplates you suffering and cannot weep—  
alas, how can such a person restrain himself?  
[Col. 0616C] O Jesus, have mercy on me, most hard-hearted.

He Is Crucified

Again, behold, O soul, those men raging against Jesus,  
violently placing him upon the harsh cross,  
horribly piercing his limbs with iron,  
and nailing Christ with extreme cruelty to the wood.

With compassion, look upon the mad crowd  
pressing the naked, tender, unsound body  
upon the rough, uneven wood,  
and piercing the beautiful hand with a thick nail.

Contemplate this long and graceful hand,  
pierced most tightly while suffering for you,  
pouring out blood most abundantly for you,  
enduring the bitterest wound for you.

[Col. 0616D] O most holy hand, pierced for me,  
badly torn by the thickness of the nail,  
cruelly lacerated by the force of the blows,  
write upon me how you have been afflicted.

Consider this, most hard-hearted one, who have never wept;  
call earnestly upon this great punishment.

You will weep if you feel Christ’s pain,  
or at least what befell his sorrowful Mother because of it.

Indeed, when the Mother saw this, she grew even weaker,  
and, violently shaken, wasted away within herself;  
with her senses almost gone, she no longer knew herself,  
but, dissolving in weeping, seemed already to melt away.

Alas for the sorrow! The terrible distress of this wound  
seems to strike the Mother with the Son’s sufferings.  
[Col. 0617A] Run, run, O soul, hasten now to go,  
so that you may support the Lady as she falls.

Alas, Lady, this is a hard day for you,  
for the rights of a mother have now surrounded you;  
now you feel more numerous evils than a woman in labor,  
which you had been spared in giving birth as a mother.

O sorrow! O groaning! Where will you turn,  
afflicted on every side by the torture of your Son?  
How will you endure the future scars,  
since you are so weakened by this piercing?

Then, while this hand was fastened in such grievous suffering,  
the other was stretched out to be nailed,  
but the holes were exceedingly irregular,  
formed beyond the length of the body.

O sorrow! O groaning! What are they now about to do?

[Col. 0617B] Let those who consider this, no longer hard of heart, groan,  
as the wicked men, hastening toward destruction,  
drag the limbs of pure Christ  
to the places of the holes.

As you have read, O soul, behold the dreadful people,  
the inhuman soldiers, alas, raging too fiercely,  
stretching the limbs of your Lord by force  
and pulling them this way and that like hides.

Who can express how much they stretched him,  
so that they almost dismembered the Lord limb by limb [Note: [Col. 0617] See Suárez, *In III partem*, vol. II, disputation 36, section 4.],  
nearly exposing all his bones,  
and piercing his limbs with the thickest nails?

Who could speak of the horror,  
or of the cruelty of those crucifying him,  
or of the Lord’s painful suffering,  
or of the anguish of his Mother and those who loved him?

[Col. 0617C] Here let our hardness be utterly broken;  
let our marrow be turned into tears of blood;  
let all our desires be fixed upon Jesus,  
and thus let our hearts be torn by powerful grief.

If we are ashamed to pass this by without weeping,  
here it is fitting for us to roar from the groaning of our hearts;  
and, when we feel sorrow with the weeping Lord,  
if he grants it, even to die with him.

Christ Weeps on the Cross

While contemplating, O soul, expand your mind here;  
see Jesus enduring the greatest pains,  
weeping in torment most bitterly for you,  
suffering wholly within and without.

Behold, his limbs are horribly stretched;  
[Col. 0617D] skin and flesh are pierced by the rough iron;  
alas, the joints of his bones are torn apart from one another,  
and all his limbs are drenched with blood.

His most tender hands are pierced by nails,  
his feet are cruelly bored through in the same way;  
his nerves are lacerated by sharp irons,  
and likewise his tender veins are torn by the nails.

See, see those innermost tortures,  
the groans and cries of his heart,  
the abundant weeping of his eyes as well,  
and how all the beauty of his body has been taken away.

O most merciful Jesus, what have you done?  
Why have you endured so many torments for wretched beings?  
[Col. 0618A] Make me be marked with this Passion;  
wound me with your wounds and your bitter death.

Again, behold, O soul, the face of the weeping Mother,  
continually present amid these anguishes;  
consider the unspeakable pains of her mind,  
almost dying under the pressure of distress.

Alas, most beautiful Virgin, ignorant of sin,  
formerly more splendid than all other women,  
now pale, mournful, and wholly bitter,  
while your beloved Child suffers before you.

I am compelled, O Lady, to remain silent about you,  
because I see you suffering more  
than any words could truly express,  
or the pure meditation of the mind comprehend.

I am not surprised, O crowned Lady, Virgin,  
[Col. 0618B] that you are placed in such grievous torments;  
but I marvel at how you persevere thus,  
and that your heart does not break as life departs.

O my confidence, I beg you, be willing  
to pierce me at once with the arrows of your pain;  
make me continually be your faithful servant,  
and let me adore my Lady in heaven.

Who can consider these things without tears:  
the Savior of God enduring so many grave sufferings,  
this Virgin Mother weeping so greatly,  
and the holy apostles enduring many things?

Apostle John, who saw these things  
and, seeing them, grieved inwardly and wept,  
obtain tears and Christ’s wounds for me;  
help me when you see me standing before Jesus.

[Col. 0618C] O loving one of the Lord, pious Magdalene,  
you who saw him suffer, filled with great grief,  
I ask you, through the manifold pain which you behold,  
obtain for me mourning and the delights of heaven.

O all the other holy women, each of you Mary,  
who saw the Messiah’s grievous torments,  
pour forth prayers for me continually to the gracious Son,  
so that he may make me safe on the last day.

By Christ’s bloody wounds, I adjure you,  
for which you offered the most sorrowful lamentations,  
help me reject the enemy’s temptations,  
and not endure eternal torments.

Now the soul, desiring the fruit of tears,  
should once again be turned wholly toward the Lord;  
now, now, pious soul, become a conduit of water;  
thereafter, if you can, melt entirely into grief.

[Col. 0618D] Look, look inwardly upon Jesus as he cries out,  
examining each of his wounds on every side,  
piously investigating how heavily they are burdened,  
and what the wicked men did when they raised up the cross.

Behold, behold, they raise the sign that was named beforehand,  
previously foretold by the prophetic Spirit:  
Jesus, true man, God, the Son of God,  
stretched and nailed most tightly upon the wood.

Groaning, behold, O soul, those raising the cross,  
finally planting it with tremendous force:  
alas, violently jolting his dislocated limbs  
[Col. 0619A] and torturing the Lord beyond expression.

Who would not mourn, seeing the fury of the wicked,  
Christ’s abundance of tears and sighs,  
and this gravest punishment of all his limbs,  
dislocated and thus violently jolted?

Run, run, O soul, now, if you are devout;  
hasten wholly and without delay to this cross;  
gather and drink the blood running down,  
and mark forever all that he suffered.

Contemplate these nails piercing his hands,  
alas, bearing the whole weight of his body,  
increasing his wounds beyond expression,  
and, as I truly judge, tearing them apart!

His neck exhausted, alas, his painful head hangs down,  
without support, bloody and crowned with thorns!

[Col. 0619B] Who would not weep, seeing that beautiful face,  
bloodied, pale, mournful, and bruised?

Certainly, whoever thinks upon these things and does not weep  
shows that he does not love God sufficiently.  
Jesus, I beg you, lavish tears upon me;  
never let me be found to love you too little.

He Prays for His Crucifiers

Jesus, who were nailed to the cross by the wicked  
and yet begged the Father’s forgiveness for them,  
have mercy on me and on believers;  
continually spare us and never be angry with us.

Again, behold, O soul, how the Jews—  
the chief priests, scribes, and Pharisees—  
cry out: “Ha! You who destroy the temple of the true God,  
save yourself, if you are the Son of God.”

[Col. 0619C] The two guilty men hanging with the Lord:  
one says to him, “Save yourself and us”;  
the other, asking for grace, says: “Remember me.”  
To him the Lord promises the paradise of God.

Most loving Jesus, who did no wrong,  
why did you undergo so many monstrous torments?  
Certainly, Lord, you endured these things for me,  
and what I stole, you paid for by suffering.

I am the one who deserved your betrayal,  
your bonds, scourging, and condemnation,  
your spitting, blows, and death;  
I am the cause of all your Passion.

I do evil, while you are punished;  
I, alas, am proud, while you are humbled;  
I laugh vainly, while you weep;  
[Col. 0619D] I eat sweet things, while you are given gall to drink.

Timid Eve, not the pious one, laughs with me;  
humble Mary weeps bitterly with you.  
I am in prosperity, while you are in agony.  
Messiah, I beg you, make me grieve with you.

Behold, his holy entrails, stretched out, dry up;  
his limbs, horribly bloodied, grow stiff;  
his eyes, clouded with tears, grow weak;  
his nectar-like lips, alas, grow pale.

O omnipotent Jesus, who discern all things,  
why do you thus despise this most holy body?  
Would it not be better not to be subjected to the lower regions  
than to enjoy the heavens while you, God, are tortured in this way?

Truly, excessive love compelled you to these things,  
[Col. 0620A] and almost reduced you to nothing;  
triumphant charity accomplished this work,  
but, alas, it has not yet broken our hardness.

O ungrateful, wicked, undevout soul,  
why are you not moved by these pains and this weeping?  
Behold, you have been washed by the Lord’s dreadful death;  
this entire Passion takes place for your vices.

It is evident, most wicked soul, that you now lack life,  
since, while contemplating him suffering, you remain so hard;  
thus, while you eat Jesus as though forgetful,  
alas, neither then nor at any other time are you truly contrite.

See the Son of God, a virtuous man,  
formerly beautiful in word and deed;  
now more disgraced than evildoers,  
called a criminal by many for your sake.

[Col. 0620B] O most merciful Jesus, who are exceedingly gracious,  
though, thinking of you suffering, I have scarcely wept,  
I beg you, most kind Lord, give me tears;  
show me how you have been wounded.

Alas for me, who cannot, through compassion,  
always carry your Passion in my heart,  
this supreme love of God toward me,  
this supreme outpouring of God’s grace.

If the faithful are called the limbs of the Lord,  
why do they not grieve with the suffering Head?  
Alas, it threatens that many are already being cut off,  
who are not seen to grieve over the Head’s pain.

I know that if my foot were badly injured,  
my whole heart would be stirred to compassion.  
Therefore the foot seems to be loved more than Christ,  
[Col. 0620C] for whose anguish one is scarcely moved!

O Jesus, who never sinned at all,  
did you not make me so that I might be joined to you?  
Why did you not permit me, the guilty one, to be wounded, Christ,  
and, alas, why did you not wound me as a guilty one together with you?

I am the one who ought to be wounded,  
not you, who have done no wickedness.  
I am guilty; the guilt is mine.  
Wound me, so that I may not be separated from you.

Pious Son, full of divine goodness,  
do not hold your wounds so tightly as someone else’s;  
your deeds are good, mine are shameful;  
be willing to wound me even by your punishment.

Ruler, Lord of heaven and earth,  
I beg you, wound me and do not delay.  
For I cannot bear my heart remaining unharmed  
while I see you endure so many wounds for me.

Is it not more pious to keep the man made by you  
subdued with you in your wounds  
than to let him depart from you, reduced to nothing,  
and deeply distracted by various thoughts?

Run, run, wounded Jesus, at this hour,  
lest you perhaps lose me if there is delay;  
grant that I may feel your greater torments;  
engrave your sharper wounds upon me.

You who permit iron to penetrate within you,  
why do you let me, a rational being, remain outside?  
Do not consider me less valuable than iron,  
but force me to enter into your wounds.

[Col. 0621A] Jesus, I beseech your mercies,  
through the merits and prayers of your Mother,  
through the intercessions of all the saints,  
so that I may continually ponder your sufferings.

Let abundant weeping for contemplating you be mine;  
let me always remember you, filled with tears.  
I pray that I may never be joyful except in you;  
be my joy and my hidden love.

Now, O soul, attend to the Virgin Mother;  
consider how greatly she suffers beneath the cross;  
offer prayers at once, so that she may wound you with her,  
and show with tears that you grieve with her.

O Mother, how greatly you are crucified inwardly  
by the Son’s multiplied torments!  
O Virgin of Christ, truly my advocate,  
[Col. 0621B] reveal something of this to me when entreated.

O my confidence and my patroness,  
shining crown of all purity,  
be present in spirit, though not in person,  
so that I may speak what you yourself teach, good Mother.

Speak now, Lady, worthy above all;  
I beg you, gracious one, do not despise the guilty!  
Quickly mark your wounds for me,  
and give words worthy of so great a subject.

But perhaps you reply that I am not such a person  
to whom you should reveal this painful misery,  
nor equal to your least servants,  
so that I might ask this special grace from you.

I know, I know, Lady, that I am unworthy.  
But what harm can it do to me who accuse myself?  
[Col. 0621C] I beseech you for God’s sake, Rod of Jesse’s stock,  
to deign to attend to my prayers.

But you say that I do not confess everything truthfully,  
nor sincerely make atonement as I have sinned;  
that I forget many things, conceal some,  
and do not repent properly by avoiding crimes.

Alas, Mother of mercy, these are harsh words,  
which, alas, are true, though bitter.  
The proud mind does not wish to be seen as it is;  
but I beg you, heal me for the sake of salvation’s words.

Behold, I confess to you all my crime;  
in every sin I confess myself guilty—  
those in which you know that I offended God—  
and I beg you to compel him to save me.

[Col. 0621D] I have sinned through pride and evil thought,  
through sight, word, deed, and omission,  
through taste, touch, smell, and hearing,  
through much negligence and pleasure.

I have offended through malice and perverse habit,  
through scant love of God and neighbor,  
through lust, greed, anger, and envy;  
through gluttony, sloth, hatred, and sluggishness.

I confess these things to you and to the Almighty,  
and to the assembly of the saints dwelling with you.  
I beseech you, by the merit of the divine torment:  
save the guilty one and grant forgiveness to him who asks.

Behold what I have often become by sinning;  
I show you, O merciful one, at least a little.  
Now I entrust all my evils to you,  
[Col. 0622A] so that you yourself may save me by taking them away.

But what am I doing, reporting the filth of my uncleanness  
to the hearing of the Virgin of supreme purity?  
I shudder, most holy Mother of mercy,  
to speak thus to your undefiled ears.

I fear lest you perhaps turn away from me  
because of the many corruptions implanted within me;  
but through Jesus I beg you to turn toward me,  
in whom you recognize so many certain wretchednesses.

You, who piously regard everyone’s prayers,  
will you alone be harsh to me, wretched as I am?  
Why do you bear the well-known name of mercy  
if you do not have mercy on me when I ask?

Do not change this custom on my account,  
by which you are accustomed to bring salvation to the wretched;  
[Col. 0622B] and do not, though I am impious, I beg you, reject me,  
but make the powers of your clemency effective in me.

Remember, Lady, perfect above all,  
that you were chosen on behalf of the guilty;  
you became the Mother of God because of the wretched.  
Therefore save the wretched, our exalted hope.

For their sake, Lady, God entered into you;  
for their sake he endured human miseries;  
for their sake, while you looked on, he grew weary in torments,  
and for them he was pressed by the anguish of death.
